channels.regime: Strong PMI/new orders and rising prices reinforce the Fed's hawkish stance.
US 10Y remains around the 5%+ danger zone, real yields are elevated and Japan's 10Y JGB printed ~3.075%, reinforcing a global duration shock.
AI/project-finance dispersion and private-credit concerns remain active; fresh CCC OAS is a gap.
Strong PMI and AI physical demand support funded capex, but financing/permitting filters tighten.
Asian crude imports have recovered to a post-war high, but remain about 13% below the pre-war average; logistics are improving without full normalisation.
Diesel futures fell to a two-week low, but policy distortion and expensive STS freight complicate the signal.
The Jan 10 trade-truce extension removes an immediate tariff cliff, but high US/Japan yields and narrow equity participation keep broad risk appetite constrained.
Gold remains tactically rate-dominated: elevated real yields and a firm dollar continue to outweigh geopolitical hedging at the margin.
SoftBank's US$11.1B bond deal proves funding access for a strong sponsor but reinforces leverage and credit-market dependence.
Trade-tail risk eased, but the external truce is not evidence of a repair in Chinese household credit, private demand or domestic transmission.
Rare-earth and critical-mineral access remains a central Trump-Xi negotiation channel with direct aerospace, semiconductor and strategic-supply implications.
Texas/EU constraints and self-supply requirements keep realizable MW below headline queues.

notes: The US-China truce extension through 10 January 2027 reduces the immediate tariff/goods-inflation tail risk, but it is not a comprehensive trade settlement.

The Trump-Xi summit is now an event-risk transmission channel for rare earths, advanced-chip controls, Chinese purchases and China-exposed US companies; exact deal text matters more than headline tone.
Japan's 10Y JGB reached about 3.075%. Japanese repatriation or reduced foreign-bond demand is a risk to monitor, not an observed flow unless holdings/flow data confirm it.
Asia crude imports recovered to about 23.96mbpd but remain roughly 13% below the pre-war average, consistent with partial logistics repair rather than full normalisation.
Real yields remain the cleanest cross-asset constraint for gold, long-duration equities and leveraged AI infrastructure.
Creator/social claims and unverified summit concessions remain zero-weight until independently verified.

forwardView.baseCase: Rates remain the dominant cross-asset constraint, but the verified US-China truce extension removes one near-term inflation and supply-chain tail risk. A durable risk-on broadening still requires US/Japan yields to stabilise and summit headlines to convert into specific, verifiable concessions.
forwardView.dollar: Bias remains firm while US growth/prices and front-end yields stay strong; trade de-escalation alone is insufficient to reverse the rates advantage.
forwardView.rates: US 10Y above 5% and Japan 10Y above 3% are the key global-duration tripwires. Treat Japanese capital repatriation as a monitored hypothesis until flow data confirm it.
forwardView.equities: Trade relief is a marginal positive, especially for China-exposed cyclicals and semis, but prefer funded/cash-generative AI and grid exposures until breadth, credit and yields improve.
forwardView.energy: Separate partial crude-flow recovery from refined-product, LNG and freight tightness. Falling geopolitical premium in one barrel does not prove product normalisation.
forwardView.gold: Tactically weak until US real yields and DXY roll over together; reclaiming the low-$4,300s would be more meaningful if rates confirm.
forwardView.nextCatalyst: Trump-Xi summit; US jobless claims and new-home sales; Treasury auction/Fed follow-through; Japan 10Y JGB persistence above 3%; exact rare-earth and advanced-chip language.
